title: VRRP and HSRP: a redundant gateway

videos.script: Every computer in an office has one default gateway. One address, where it sends everything that is not local. {{gateway}} Put a second router in the office and nothing changes for the computers. They still send to the first one. When it dies, the office is offline, with a healthy router sitting right next to it. {{dead}} VRRP fixes this by making the gateway's address move. Two routers share one virtual address. One of them holds it, and tells the other every second that it is still alive. {{adverts}} In this lesson you set it up with keepalived on the head office routers. You watch the election, and the advertisements on the wire. {{election}} Then you pull a cable and measure the gap, with a ping every fifth of a second. Fifteen replies go missing, a little over three seconds. {{gap}} You watch the first router take its address back when the cable returns. And you watch it give the address away when its internet link goes down, because a gateway with no way out is worse than none. {{track}} Last, you meet HSRP and GLBP, Cisco's versions of the same idea, and what they do differently. {{cisco}}
